chapter: Sidemen, mixed bands, the Apollo and Lena Horne
title: Sitting in with Ellington at the Casa Manana in 1943
summary: Barnet tried to get Ellington's band drunk, then played a whole set in Otto Hardwick's chair, with a finale involving both bands.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: For sure. Chilton mentions that you once depped -- that must be a British term for subbed -- on alto for Otto Hardwick, with Duke Ellington on the 6th of March, 1943.

This was at the Casa Manana. In fact I have a picture of that. A picture of me sitting in the Ellington section with Johnny Hodges on one side and Harry Carney on the other and the other guys. The Ellington Band and my band -- Joe Zuka, who had the Casa Manana, I was sort of the house band in there, you know, and he said, 'I've got Duke Ellington coming in,' he said, 'I'm going to have you both here for the weekend.' I said, 'Oh, great, wonderful.' So now we're plotting backstage, we're going to have to subdue them, so we adopted a policy we were going to get them drunk. Now, they had the Red Callendar Trio to play while the bands were changing position on the stage, because there was only room for one band on the stage. So Toby, you know, he went pretty good -- that's Otto Hardwick -- and he got a little out of it, and Duke came out there just as I was giving him a drink, you know, and he looked at me, and if looks could kill I would have gone right through the floor. He says, 'So.' Okay. So I got real guilty. I said, 'Gee.' Toby was -- he really couldn't go out. He had had it. So I went out and I said, 'Boss, can I help you out here a little bit?' And he says, 'Go ahead, sit down.' And so I wound up playing the whole set with Duke that night.

And we had a rousing finale with both bands on stage and everybody, a whole bunch of musicians, Wingy Manone jumped up there, Corky Corcoran, I mean everybody in the joint. I've got a picture of this, home.

Everybody playing, and I think we were playing "C Jam Blues." I don't know. Maybe that was before "C Jam Blues." We were playing some kind of blues. And we had a ball. And Joe -- you know who played most of the night? Red Callendar. Because the bands would get together in the back and they were all drinking together and everything, and Joe Zuka came back and he said, "I'm paying for two big bands, what have I got? I've got a stinking trio out here playing. Now get somebody on this bandstand," you know. And it was really a rather humorous situation. That band room was just like a nightclub.
It sounds like a very special night.
